newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi foreign reserves seen $11.8 bln at year-end.
newsitem.headline: Saudi foreign reserves seen $11.8 bln at year-end.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's foreign reserves have risen to their highest level since 1991 and are likely to grow to $11.8 billion by the end of the year, a leading Saudi-based economist said in a report published on Monday.
The study by Jeddah-based National Commercial Bank's chief economist Henry Azzam said the kingdom was expected to drawdown its reserves to help finance the current account deficit.

"Foreign reserves rose to their highest level since 1991. By the end of June 1996, total reserves were reported to the IMF (International Monetary Fund) at $10 billion, up by 16 percent from the $8.6 billion at the end of 1995," he said.
"Foreign reserves...are likely to end the year at $11.8 billion," Azzam said.
Azzam said Saudi Arabia's overall financial position has improved in 1996 due mainly to higher oil prices.

Analysts expect the state to use the extra oil revenue to build up the foreign reserves, which were run down after the Gulf war, pay back debts to contractors and suppliers and reduce the need for domestic debt to help finance the deficit.
Economists in the kingdom forecast a current account deficit of $2 billion to $2.5 billion, about half that of 1995.
"A noticeable improvement in the kingdom's external balances is expected this year, with the current account deficit dropping to $2 billion," Azzam said in the study.

"A larger current account deficit is forecast for 1997 because of projected weaker oil prices; however, the deficit will easily be financed from private capital inflows and the drawdown on foreign reserves accumulated in 1996."
Saudi Arabia's King Fahd said on Sunday his government was committed to pressing ahead with development plans, protecting its citizens against economic hardships and meeting payments to contractors.
He said in an interview with the official Saudi Press Agency, published late on Sunday to mark the kingdom's national day on Monday, that the Saudi economy was "strong and has a solid basis.
